summary: V. R. Srinivasan works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi, attested in 2026.

Indologist V. Raghavan (1908–1979) studied at Presidency College, Chennai, and the University of Madras under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He worked at the University of Madras (1934–1968) and served as secretary of the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (~1944–1979).
Vaibhav Singh works in Indology and history/archaeology. He completed a PhD at the University of Reading by 2017 and held a post there, attested in 2018.
Valaiyattur Venkayya (1864–1912) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras. He succeeded Eugen Hultzsch.

Valdo H. Viglielmo (1926–2016) was a scholar of Japanology and philosophy. Educated at Harvard, the University of Tokyo, and Gakushuin University, he held posts at Harvard, Princeton, and the University of Hawaiʻi (1965–2002).

Valeria Gazizova specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. She completed her master's degree at the University of Oslo, studying under Hanna Havnevik and supervisor Per Kvaerne (attested 2009).

Van Austin Harvey (1926–2021) was a religious studies scholar educated at Occidental College and Yale University. He held positions at Princeton, Perkins School of Theology, the University of Pennsylvania, and Stanford University (~1978–1996).
Vans Kennedy (1784–1846) worked in Indology and linguistics. He served as judge-advocate-general in the Bombay Army (1817–1835) and as president of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1835–1846).

Vasant Shivram Shinde is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts as Professor and Professor of South Asian Archaeology at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, attested in 2006 and 2026.

Sinologist Vasily Mikhaylovich Alekseyev (1881–1951) studied at St. Petersburg University and under Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1910–1951) and the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences (~1918–1951).

Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev (1818–1900) was a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Kazan Federal University under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski and served as professor at Kazan Federal University and Saint Petersburg State University.

Vasily Radlov (1837–1918) was a linguist, archaeologist, and Central Asian specialist. After studying at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Jena, he served as director of the Asiatic Museum (1885–1890) and the Kunstkamera (1894–1918).

Vasily Seseman (1884–1963) was a philosopher who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1903–1909). He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1915–1918), Vytautas Magnus University (~1923–1940), and Vilnius University (~1940–1950).

Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale (1901–1991) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Bonn. He held academic posts at Fergusson College, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Delhi.

Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi (1893–1985) was an Indologist and archaeologist. Educated at Deccan College and the University of Mumbai, he served as Principal of Morris College and later held a professorship at Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University (1957–1966).

Vasudeva Sharan Agrawala (1904–1967) was an Indologist and archaeologist educated at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Lucknow. He served as curator of Mathura Museum, director of State Museum Lucknow, and Department Head at Banaras Hindu University.

Indologist Vasudha Dalmia studied at Miranda House, the University of Cologne, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Heidelberg University. She held teaching positions at the University of Tübingen, UC Berkeley (2001–2012), and Yale University (2013–2014).

Vasudha Narayanan is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at the universities of Madras, Mumbai, and Harvard. She served as Distinguished Professor of Religion at the University of Florida and president of the American Academy of Religion.

Vatroslav Jagić (1838–1923) was a linguist who studied at the University of Vienna (~1856–1860). He held posts at Odesa University, Humboldt University of Berlin, Imperial St. Petersburg University, and the University of Vienna (~1886–1908).

Veeranarayana N. K. Pandurangi specializes in Indology, philosophy, and computational fields. He studied at Central and National Sanskrit Universities, teaching at Poornaprajna Vidyapeetha, Rajasthan Sanskrit University, and Karnataka Samskrit University (attested 2020).
